value: Provides the generalized HSD_GObj constructor used by the standard GObj_Create wrapper: it allocates a game object, establishes a neutral unattached initial state, and inserts it into a selected process-link list using a caller-selected priority or position-relative placement mode.

value: Asserts that p_link is in range and returns NULL if allocation fails. On success, the object begins with no GX link, attached object, process chain, render callback, HSD object, or user data. Mode 0 inserts after existing objects of equal priority, mode 1 inserts before existing objects of equal priority, mode 2 inserts after position, and mode 3 inserts before position.
rationale: The current body explicitly establishes the assertion, failure branch, and neutral initial fields. The two priority helpers use strict comparisons, causing mode 0 to retain equal-priority objects before the new object and mode 1 to insert before the first equal-priority object; modes 2 and 3 pass position or position->prev to the insert-after primitive.

evidence.why: Shows the strict priority searches, range assertion, allocation-failure path, neutral field state, and all four placement selections.

value: Provides the standard three-argument constructor for an HSD_GObj, creating an initialized object and inserting it into the selected process-link list according to process priority.
rationale: The current wrapper delegates directly to CreateGObj with ordinary mode-0 placement. That callee allocates and initializes the object, then searches the chosen process-link list by priority before insertion.

value: Asserts that p_link is within HSD_GObjLibInitData.p_link_max and returns NULL on allocation failure. On success, it creates an object with no GX link, attached object, processes, render callback, HSD object, or user data, then inserts it into nondecreasing p_priority order after already-present objects of equal priority.
rationale: GObj_Create selects mode 0. The callee's mode-0 search starts from the bucket tail and moves backward only while an existing priority is strictly greater, so the resulting insertion follows entries whose priorities are lower than or equal to the new priority, including existing ties.

evidence.why: Shows the wrapper's mode-0 selection together with the assertion, failure path, neutral initialization, and priority insertion behavior.

value: Reads gobj->p_link to select a process-link bucket and consumes hiprio_gobj as the insertion predecessor. It writes gobj->prev and gobj->next, updates either hiprio_gobj->next or the bucket head in HSD_GObj_Entities, then updates either the successor's prev pointer or the bucket tail in plinklow_gobjs.
rationale: Every input and write is explicit in the function body. The two conditional pairs cover the four boundary combinations required to splice an object into a doubly linked list without traversal.

evidence.why: Shows the bucket-index read and all object, neighbor, head, and tail pointer writes performed by the insertion.

value: void (HSD_GObj* gobj, HSD_GObj* hiprio_gobj), where gobj is the object being inserted and hiprio_gobj is a nullable predecessor in the same process-link bucket; NULL denotes insertion at the bucket head.

value: Inserts an HSD_GObj into its process-link bucket immediately after a supplied predecessor, serving as the common doubly linked-list insertion primitive used when creating a game object or assigning it a new process-link position.
rationale: The current primitive selects the bucket from gobj->p_link and splices the object after the supplied predecessor, or at the head when that predecessor is NULL. Both construction and existing-object reassignment still route their priority-selected or position-relative placement through it.

Shows the existing-object reassignment routine invoking GObj_PReorder after unlinking and updating the object's process-link placement fields.

value: Handles list boundaries by treating a NULL predecessor as insertion at the bucket head and a NULL resulting successor as insertion at the bucket tail. value: Consumes a placement mode, an existing HSD_GObj, a new process-link index and priority, and an optional reference object. Unless deferred, it removes each attached HSD_GObjProc from the global scheduler and reverses their child links into a temporary chain, clears gobj->proc, repairs the old bucket's neighboring, head, and tail pointers, writes gobj->p_link and gobj->p_priority, inserts the object into the selected bucket, and reinserts every saved process. During active-callback deferral, the same inputs are instead copied into HSD_GObj_804CE3E4 for later execution.
rationale: The target explicitly records deferred inputs or performs each object-list and process-chain mutation. The current process helper definitions confirm that HSD_GObjProc_8038FC18 detaches global scheduler links and HSD_GObjProc_8038FAA8 reinserts the process according to its owning GObj's process link while restoring the owner's process-chain head.

evidence.why: Shows deferred-parameter storage, process-chain reversal, old-bucket unlinking, new placement fields, insertion dispatch, and process reinsertion.
Shows process insertion deriving scheduler placement from the owning GObj's p_link and restoring the GObj's process-chain head.

value: If the requested object is the GObj whose process callback is currently executing and deferred operations are not already being drained, relocation is postponed until that callback returns. Otherwise, mode 0 places the object after existing equal-priority objects, mode 1 places it before existing equal-priority objects, mode 2 inserts it after position, and mode 3 inserts it before position. After process reinsertion, the routine also normalizes affected processes' three-state invocation-generation markers from the older computed generation to the immediately preceding generation.
rationale: The target's guard stores a pending request instead of mutating the active object, and the process runner drains that request after on_invoke returns. The current priority helpers retain strict comparisons that determine tie placement, while the target's modulo-three calculations and conditional flags_3 write establish the generation-marker transition.

evidence.why: Shows the active-object deferral guard, all four placement modes, modulo-three generation calculations, and the conditional flags_3 transition.

Shows the scheduler marking the active GObj, invoking its process callback, and draining the saved relocation request afterward.

Removal and relinking rewrite neighboring objects and the corresponding head or tail entry.
rationale: At head, creation still passes gobj_alloc_data to HSD_ObjAlloc and initializes the returned object. Every insertion, removal, and reassignment path still updates prev, next, the selected HSD_GObj_Entities head, and the corresponding plinklow_gobjs tail for the object's process-link bucket.

Shows complementary head, tail, and neighboring-object writes during deletion and process-link reassignment.

value: Supports four placement modes: priority insertion searched from the list's lower-priority side, priority insertion searched from its higher-priority side, insertion after a specified object, and insertion before it. Destruction or relinking of the currently executing GObj is deferred by recording pending-operation flags and, for relinking, the requested placement mode, process link, priority, and relative position.
rationale: The current constructor and reassignment routine retain placement cases 0 through 3 and use the same priority-search or relative-insertion helpers. Destruction and reassignment still guard the currently executing GObj and save pending work instead of mutating the active traversal.
